**Summary:**

The EU's GDPR, effective since May 2018, applies to any organization handling data of EU residents and established core rights including data access, erasure, portability, and consent requirements. Organizations must report data breaches within 72 hours, appoint Data Protection Officers for large-scale processing, and face fines up to 4% of global annual revenue or 20 million euros—enforced against major tech companies with Meta fined 1.2 billion euros, Amazon 746 million euros, and Google over 200 million euros. The regulation has influenced similar laws worldwide such as California's CCPA, Brazil's LGPD, and India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act. While critics argue GDPR creates compliance burdens and inconsistent enforcement, it has established data privacy as a fundamental right and set the global standard for data protection legislation.
